answer: Stake-slashing on inactivity resists sybils: an identity's bond is slowly slashed if it fails to produce genuine work each epoch, so a dormant fake held only to inflate head count bleeds its deposit toward nothing. A willow-field of idle sybils each loses nectar from its bond every quiet epoch; only an identity climbing toward the summit of real contribution keeps its stake whole. An attacker cannot cheaply warehouse a reserve army of fakes — passivity itself is penalized, converting an idle swarm into a steady capital drain.
